exposure: mode of birth (vaginal delivery, cesarean section)
cohort: All women who delivered vaginally or via cesarean section at a tertiary maternity hospital in Slovenia between 2008 and 2024 and subsequently required medical assessment or hospitalization within six weeks postpartum.
finding: Postpartum infections remain a leading complication, particularly after cesarean delivery, with specific types of complications varying by mode of birth.
mod_finding: Postpartum complications were more frequent after cesarean delivery (10.6%) than after vaginal birth (7.6%), with breast complications common after vaginal birth and surgical site complications predominant after cesarean section.
